clue.text: Places of retirement I'd find dull

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word for places is read backwards

parts.note: to place something is to put it, so places means puts
the contraction I'd is written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone finds the usual spots for growing old rather boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Places' looks like a noun (retirement homes) but is a verb, PUTS; 'retirement' turns it round to STUP. Add ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and dull are synonyms for slow-witted or tedious.

clue.text: Sun protection for a small shark, note

parts.note: the tope is a small shark of European waters
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A notice about providing shade for a little shark.
explanation.definitionFit: A topee is a lightweight pith helmet worn against the heat of the tropics.

clue.text: Who gets by late? He does!'

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
late can mean former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A question about who manages to arrive behind time, with an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: one who 'does', puts on an act.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor or entertainer is one who acts or puts on a show.

clue.text: Man offended, demanding rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise is the word read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to offend is to sin, so offended means sinned

explanation.surface: An offended man asks for a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offended' looks like an adjective (insulted) but means SINNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis is a male first name.

clue.text: Detaches shoots?

definitions.meaning: removes, pulls away a bit at a time
fires at and hits one target after another

explanation.surface: A question about what a gardener does when removing young growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Picks off means removes one piece at a time, and also means to shoot targets one by one, as a sniper does.

clue.text: In Paris real lamb is cooked for dancers

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored, worked into a new form

explanation.surface: French lamb being prepared for a ballet company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is part of the anagram, not a link; 'is' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Prima ballerinas are the leading female dancers of a ballet company.

clue.text: Someone made into a mere puppet

definitions.meaning: a being brought into existence, something created
someone wholly controlled by another, a tool

explanation.surface: A person turned into the tool of another.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any created being, and also a person entirely dependent on a patron.

clue.text: Shots also exchanged — about five

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
exchanged means the letters swap places

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Gunfire traded back and forth at about five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' turns ALSO into SALO, written 'about' V.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of gunfire, many guns firing together.

clue.text: Lee turns up in the country — he's self-employed

indicators.note: in puts the reversed name inside the country

parts.note: France is the country, a typical crossword nation

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the name from the bottom to the top

explanation.surface: A man called Lee arrives in the countryside, working for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: LEE turned up gives EEL, set inside FRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works for themself, selling services to many clients.

clue.text: He's bound to be in training

definitions.text: He's bound to be in training

parts.words: He's bound to be in training
parts.note: bound reads as certain to be, but also as tied by an indenture to a master while learning a trade

explanation.definitionFit: A trainee bound by indentures to an employer is a learner of a craft.

clue.text: Nothing backward about East — that's right !

indicators.note: about means the reversed letters go round the next piece
backward tells us the word for nothing is read in reverse order

parts.note: nil means nothing, a zero score

explanation.surface: An exclamation agreeing that nothing is behind the East.
explanation.walkthrough: NIL read backward gives LIN, which goes 'about' E.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Girl finds another carrying on in charge

indicators.note: carrying means the first name holds the next pieces within it

parts.note: Vera is another girl's name, so another girl stands for it

explanation.surface: A girl discovers that a second woman is still running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another girl, VERA, which carries ON and IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a female first name.

clue.text: Sings in theatre's opening turns

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from the theatre word

parts.note: rolls are turns, as a ship rolls or a wheel turns

explanation.surface: Someone performs songs as the curtain goes up at the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is an old word for singing in a full, carefree voice, as in a round.

clue.text: The best job we could pick ?

definitions.text: The best job we could pick

parts.words: The best job we could pick
parts.note: reads as choosing a career, but a fruit is also picked from a tree, and a top post is called by that fruit's name

explanation.definitionFit: A plum job is a highly desirable post, and the plum is a fruit picked from trees.

clue.text: He would see what we mean, no doubt

definitions.text: He would see what we mean, no doubt

parts.words: He would see what we mean, no doubt
parts.note: see what we mean usually means understand, but here it is literal: he sees our words formed on the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person may follow speech by watching the movement of the mouth.

clue.text: Poison I left for Ena to carry back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is then read in reverse
to carry means the name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A woman named Ena is asked to bring a poison home.
explanation.walkthrough: ENA carrying I and PORT gives ENIPORTA; 'back' turns it all round.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade.

clue.text: Airman takes it to fish rising-appears workable

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: LAC is a leading aircraftman in the RAF
the carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A pilot goes fishing and the plan seems feasible.
explanation.walkthrough: LAC + IT + CARP is LACITCARP; 'rising' turns all of it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something practical can be done in practice, so it is feasible.

clue.text: The way I get in fuel and drinks

indicators.note: get in means these letters go inside the word for fuel

parts.note: coals are a fuel for fires
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone describes buying petrol and refreshments on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordials are sweet fruit drinks or liqueurs.

clue.text: Moby Dick contained a new promise — money

indicators.note: new tells us the word promise is made into a new arrangement

parts.note: L, from the Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A white whale is fitted with a fresh promise of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Moby Dick is the sperm whale of Melville's novel; the definition is what that whale held.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm whales hold a waxy oil in their heads, prized for lamps and candles.

clue.text: Like holding church services, perhaps

indicators.note: holding says the word for like goes round the church letters

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone seems to be attending church worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' is not church worship but tennis serves; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an unreturnable serve is an ace, so these are examples of serves.

clue.text: Was associated with Pickwick and Weller

definitions.text: Was associated with Pickwick and Weller

parts.words: Was associated with Pickwick and Weller
parts.note: Mr Pickwick and his servant Weller in Dickens's Pickwick Papers share the same first name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' reads as a verb but goes with the first name both men bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens gave both the hero of The Pickwick Papers and his servant this Old Testament prophet's name.

clue.text: Thought as the Manx judge did ?

definitions.meaning: a judge on the Isle of Man is a deemster, so what he did is jokingly to deem

explanation.surface: A question about how a judge on the Isle of Man made up his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to consider, and the Isle of Man's judges are called deemsters, as if from deeming.

clue.text: Artist one found in the mount

indicators.note: found in means the number goes inside the next piece

parts.note: Mt is the abbreviation for mount, as in Mt Everest

explanation.surface: A painter discovers one of his works in the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of water lilies.

clue.text: Extremely hot resorts Iran's gut

indicators.note: resorts is read as re-sorts, sorting the letters again into a new order

parts.note: the fodder is the printed words with the possessive S kept as a letter, and with O for the U the page shows, since the setter meant got

explanation.surface: Scorching holiday spots are what Iran possesses.
explanation.walkthrough: Re-sorting IRANSGOT gives the answer; the page prints 'gut' for 'got', a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting describes heat fierce enough to cook meat.

clue.text: Girl put in standard A

parts.note: a norm is a standard or average

explanation.surface: A girl is placed in the top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female first name.

clue.text: -Some food intended for a god ?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question whether a dish is meant as an offering to a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Crane's wrong about name for newscasters

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the word for name
wrong says the bird's letters are set out in a mistaken order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is used as a letter here
a noun is a naming word in grammar

explanation.surface: A man called Crane has got a name wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns CRANES into ANCERS, written 'about' NOUN after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters who read the news on air are called by this title.

clue.text: Player tries to make expressions of dissent

parts.note: a pro is a professional player
tests are tries, attempts or trials

explanation.surface: A sportsman makes trial runs to voice objections.
explanation.definitionFit: Protests are formal objections or complaints.

clue.text: She is ill-disposed to Scot

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of ill are set out afresh

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A woman dislikes a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-disposed' looks like one word meaning hostile; split it, ILL rearranged ('disposed') gives LIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilian is a female first name, so it stands for a woman.
